title: Capacity E2E load framework and customer validation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Deliver an end-to-end, reproducible load and validation framework for Dedicated capacity that produces defensible throughput guarantees, verifies autoscaling policies, and provides a customer-facing acceptance test suite. Scope: load generator harness, benchmarking methodology, experiment matrix, analysis scripts, runbook for customer-facing validation runs, and integration with Console dashboards and CI. Out of scope: wholesale changes to autoscaler algorithms (those are follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Automated harness can run the three canonical load profiles (steady-state, spike, ramp) against a Dedicated pool with configurable qps/tokens/sec and duration
Benchmarking reports include p50/p95/p99 latency, tail token latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, CPU, memory, and error-rate with baseline vs candidate comparison
Autoscaling scenarios validate scale-up and scale-down behavior with configurable headroom and cooldown and assert no more than X% request errors during transitions (X=1%)
Customer acceptance checklist (scripted) runs without manual intervention and produces a signed report (PDF) with pass/fail verdict and telemetry links
All runs are reproducible via a single CLI invocation and stored in our artifacts bucket with metadata (commit, config, region, model, seed)
Runbook documents thresholds and troubleshooting steps for common failure modes (cache warm, model OOM, networking headroom)
test_matrix: Models: small/medium/large open models + quantized variants
Concurrency profiles: single long-lived stream, many short requests, mixed
Load profiles: steady (10m warm, 30m run), spike (instant + decay), ramp (linear to peak over 10m), poisson arrivals
Autoscaler configs: aggressive (fast scale), conservative (slow scale), fixed headroom (10/30/50%)
Fleet topologies: single-pool, multi-pool with routing fallback, regional failover
harness_architecture: A lightweight Python harness (loadctl) orchestrates distributed workers (k8s jobs) that emit requests to the Dedicated endpoint. Each worker collects local metrics (latency histograms, token counts, GPU stats via nvidia-smi exporter) and streams them to a central aggregator (Prometheus pushgateway compatible). Harness supports recorded-replay traffic, synthetic templates, and a small traffic recorder for live-capture. Configs are YAML with explicit knobs: model, instance type, batch size, kv-cache warm policy, seed, and warmup duration.
runbook_steps: 1) Prepare: pin model version and commit config to bench-configs repo
2) Provision: create Dedicated pool with targeted instance sku and capacity commit
3) Warmup: run KV-cache warm phase at 10% target QPS for 10 minutes
4) Baseline: execute baseline run (steady) and collect artifacts
5) Candidate: apply autoscaler variant or runtime change and execute identical run
6) Spike/Ramp: run transient scenarios and observe scale events and error rates
7) Collect: aggregate metrics, traces, and GPU telemetry into artifacts bucket
8) Analyze: run analysis script to produce summarized PDF and JSON report
9) Customer validation: execute scripted acceptance checklist with customer on a reserved pool, share run artifacts and post-run dashboard link
10) Sign-off: Product/Eng/SRE review report and tag release if passed
metrics_definitions: tokens_per_second: total generated tokens / active_seconds (excludes client think time)
request_p50_p95_p99: latency from request ingress to first-byte/last-byte as needed
tail_token_latency: latency to produce the 95th token in a generation stream for long outputs
error_rate: proportion of requests with 5xx, 4xx, or model runtime errors
gpu_utilization: average GPU util over run and 95th-percentile across instances
cache_hit_rate: KV cache hit ratio (prefix evictions recorded)
scale_events: timestamps and delta of pool size on autoscaler triggers
cost_estimate: incremental cost per hour for the Dedicated pool during the run (cloud cost + infra overhead)
